symbols.name: DOC_GLOBS
symbols.note: Tuple of glob patterns for documentation files: docs/**/*.md and README.md.

symbols.name: _INLINE_CODE
symbols.note: Regex to match single-backtick inline code spans.

symbols.name: _FENCE
symbols.note: Regex to match fenced code block delimiters.

symbols.name: _LIST_MARKER
symbols.note: Regex to match list markers to avoid misinterpreting indented list continuations as code blocks.

symbols.name: _PLACEHOLDER
symbols.note: Regex to detect placeholder characters like *?<>[]{} or ellipsis.

symbols.name: _DOTTED
symbols.note: Regex for dotted references: at least two segments, first lower-case-ish.

symbols.name: _PATH_SYMBOL
symbols.note: Regex for path::symbol or path:symbol references.

symbols.name: _PATH_ONLY
symbols.note: Regex for bare in-repo module path ending in .py.

symbols.name: _MODULE_DUNDERS
symbols.note: Frozenset of module dunder attributes that exist at runtime but not in source.

symbols.name: _FILE_EXTENSIONS
symbols.note: Frozenset of file extensions to avoid misinterpreting as Python attributes.

symbols.name: _NON_MODULE_DOTTED_NAMES
symbols.note: Frozenset of known false-positive dotted names that are not module-symbol references.

symbols.name: Reference
symbols.note: Dataclass representing one documentation reference to code.

symbols.name: reference_key
symbols.note: Returns a string key for a reference excluding line number.

symbols.name: DocRefReport
symbols.note: Dataclass holding the measurement results: resolving, broken, skipped references.

symbols.name: FixVerdict
symbols.note: Dataclass representing a fix verdict with ok flag and details.

symbols.name: iter_doc_files
symbols.note: Returns sorted, deduplicated tuple of Paths for all doc files in repo.

symbols.name: _strip_code_blocks
symbols.note: Strips fenced code blocks and indented code lines, returns prose lines and drop count.

claims.text: DOC_GLOBS: tuple[str, ...] = ("docs/**/*.md", "README.md")
claims.why: The constant is defined exactly as claimed.

claims.text: An inline-code span. Deliberately single-backtick only: a fenced block is a transcript or an example, and examples name symbols that were never meant to exist.
claims.why: The comment matches the regex definition: single backticks only, no newline.

claims.text: A fence opener/closer in markdown.
claims.why: The regex matches three or more backticks or tildes with optional whitespace.

claims.text: A list marker, so an indented list continuation is not mistaken for an indented code block.
claims.why: The regex matches list markers like -, *, +, numbered lists, and blockquotes.

claims.text: Characters that mean the reference is a PATTERN, not a name: a glob, a placeholder, an ellipsis.
claims.why: The regex matches *, ?, <, >, [, ], {, }, and ellipsis.

claims.text: A dotted reference: at least two segments, first segment lower-case-ish so Path.resolve and prose like Foo.bar do not enter as module paths.
claims.why: The regex requires at least one dot, first segment starts with lowercase letter or underscore, subsequent segments start with letter or underscore.

claims.text: path/to/mod.py::symbol and path/to/mod.py:symbol. The colon form requires an IDENTIFIER after it, so daedalus/cli.py:794 (a line number) is not read as a symbol that is missing.
claims.why: The regex matches .py followed by :: or : and then an identifier starting with letter or underscore.

claims.text: A bare in-repo module path, no symbol.
claims.why: The regex matches paths ending in .py with allowed characters.

claims.text: Attributes every module has at runtime that no source line declares. Asking ast whether daedalus defines __file__ gets the answer no, which is true of the SOURCE and false of the module.
claims.why: The frozenset includes common dunder attributes like __file__, __name__, etc.

claims.text: A dotted reference whose last segment is one of these is a FILENAME, not an attribute.
claims.why: The frozenset includes many file extensions like md, rs, json, etc.

claims.text: Dotted inline-code spans that are demonstrably NOT module-symbol references. These are measured corpus ambiguities, not a general vocabulary blacklist
claims.why: The frozenset contains 'core.autocrlf' and 'status.code' as claimed.

claims.text: The identity of a reference ACROSS an edit. Deliberately excludes the line number: correcting a sentence above moves every reference below it, and a key that moved with them would report the original finding as withdrawn for every unrelated edit in the file.
claims.why: The function returns f"{ref.doc_path}|{ref.raw}" which excludes line number.

claims.text: Every prose file in the corpus, sorted, deduplicated.
claims.why: The function collects files from DOC_GLOBS, sorts, and deduplicates via set conversion and sorted.

claims.text: Return [(line_no, line)] for prose lines, plus how many were dropped. Two kinds of code are dropped: fenced blocks, and lines indented four or more spaces that are not list continuations.
claims.why: The docstring describes exactly what the function returns and the two kinds of code dropped; the function signature matches.
